parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hi Shona.

Hi Peter, have you made up your mind about which internship program to apply for?

Yes, pretty much.

I’m entirely at a loss. I mean, there are so many good ones. Can you give me some tips?

Sure. What is your top priority when weighing up these programs?

Well, I guess I’d go for ones that can help me with the skill set I lack for my future career. I still need a lot of practical training in dealing with statistics. But keep in mind that you don’t want to set your goals too grand, like drawing up a business plan, you might end up nowhere.

I see. So I want to learn how to organize ideas and present them.

Good. Now you’ve nailed step one.

Now what?

You must also consider your strengths for a suitable internship program. Otherwise, you might get rejected or end up with one that you are incapable of doing.

But I have no idea what I’m good at.

Communicate with people around you or whom you’ve worked with. That’s what I did. I thought I was a good team leader. But many people I’ve worked with for various projects mentioned something else. They admired that I could stick to the schedule to finish projects on time. And indeed, I’m more focused and perform better when I’m pushed for time.

Good point. So what do you plan to do next?

I’ll visit the careers officer to help me with the general application form. You know, the one we have to submit before applying to companies.

But it is unnecessary to fill it in. It’s only optional.

Really? I’m glad I heard from you. Then I’ll ask the careers officer to look at my personal statement, and give me some tips on polishing it up.

Don’t you need help with your CV?

No, I’m good. I have already learned to write it in class.

That’s good. So what kind of company did you choose?

I’ve decided to apply for an IT company.

Why is that?

Well, even though I’ve learned how the IT industry developed in the past, from different lectures, I know nothing about its latest trends. I’m prepared to work in an IT company to keep up with the latest trends.

I see. What do you plan to do next term?

I think I’ll stick to most of the optional modules I’ve chosen. But regarding the language sessions, I’m doing poorly in Japanese. I’d better drop it before wasting more time. I think I’ll learn Spanish instead.

Oh, I learned Spanish for a year. I think you’ll find it interesting.

Do you know what job opportunities these companies offer in turns?

I’ve searched online and browsed some of the schemes. Do you know S-A-G?

Yes, I heard they offer internship positions, dealing with customer relationship management. But I’m not quite sure what that means.

Well, the position offers the chance to become fully aware of customer retention and keep in touch with customers to keep them highly engaged and satisfied. These include activities such as PR, communications, marketing and customer service.

Sounds like loads of work to do. What about Gemini Technologies?

It’s an IT consulting company. Although many employees say it’s stressful working there, I want to apply for this one.

Why is that?

Actually, the company provides service to improve software architecture. But that’s pretty demanding as a team of software engineers has to provide detailed analysis and suggestions for required changes before the deadline. As an observer and participant of a particular project, an intern can learn how to work to a strict deadline.

That’s not my area of expertise, but I’m sure you’ll excel at this.

I certainly do hope so. Have you checked out Deloitte?

Of course, that’s a renowned accounting firm. And thus, its internships offer excellent learning experiences in this regard. You know, things like examining a company’s financial statements, the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement. I want to give it a try, but I might get rejected, so I need a backup plan.

Have you read anything about Kearney?

Yes, it is another consulting firm. It provides opportunities to reach out to other business partners and pay attention to networking.

Well, that sounds interesting. I’m thinking about Vortex. But I haven’t got anything useful from its website.

I worked there last summer. It’s an international company, with headquarters in Spain. So most of the managers here speak Spanish. Thanks to the internship experience, I became fluent in it.

Right. That’s not for me.

questions.question: What skills does Peter want to learn?

analyses.content: Peter 明确表示，为了未来的职业生涯，他缺乏且需要针对性训练的技能是处理统计数据（dealing with statistics）。
Peter: I still need a lot of practical training in dealing with statistics.
A 选项（organize ideas）是 Peter 后来的想法，但 Shona 提醒那是第一步，而 Peter 最开始强调的短板是统计学；C 选项（business plan）是 Shona 劝阻他不要设定的过大目标。

options.option: He can communicate well with many people.
options.optionContent: He can communicate well with many people.

analyses.content: Peter: ...I thought I was a good team leader. But many people I’ve worked with for various projects mentioned something else. They admired that I could stick to the schedule... and indeed, I’m more focused and perform better when I’m pushed for time. Shona: ...Although many employees say it’s stressful working there... I’m sure you’ll excel at this.
选项 A 是最大的干扰项，原文中彼得说“I thought I was a good team leader”（我原以为我是个好领导），但紧接着用“But... mentioned something else”（但是别人指出了其他的）进行了自我否定。
文中彼得（Peter）提到自己在“时间紧迫”（pushed for time）时表现更好，且肖娜（Shona）确信他能在一家“压力大”（stressful）、“要求高”（demanding）且有“严格截止日期”（strict deadline）的公司表现出色，这对应了能承受高压/长时间工作的能力。

questions.question: What will the careers officer help Peter with?

analyses.content: Peter: Then I’ll ask the careers officer to look at my personal statement, and give me some tips on polishing it up.
C 选项（Application form）Peter 原本想去，但 Shona 说是非必须的（unnecessary）；A 选项（CV）Peter 说已经在课上学过了，不需要帮忙。
Peter 决定去找职业官员看他的**个人陈述（personal statement）**并寻求润色建议。

options.option: to update his knowledge in the area
options.optionContent: to update his knowledge in the area

questions.question: Why did Peter choose the IT business?

analyses.content: Peter: I’m prepared to work in an IT company to keep up with the latest trends.
"Keep up with latest trends" 对应选项 A 中的 "update knowledge"。C 选项（prepare for lectures）与原文相反，他是把 Lecture 里没学到的补上。
Peter 选择 IT 公司是因为他对该行业的**最新趋势（latest trends）**一无所知，想通过实习来跟上这些趋势。

questions.question: What will Peter do for the next term?

analyses.content: Peter: I’d better drop it... I think I’ll learn Spanish instead.
A 选项是继续，C 选项是彻底放弃，Peter 是 "Spanish instead"，属于更换（Change）。
Peter 打算退掉（drop）日语课，改为学习西班牙语（learn Spanish instead），即换一门语言。

analyses.content: SAIC (文中拼写为 S-A-G) 提供的职位涉及客户关系管理（customer relationship management）。
Shona: ...dealing with customer relationship management.
原文直接提到 "customer relationship management" 和 "customer retention"，对应选项 B。
Shona: ...an intern can learn how to work to a strict deadline.
"Work to a strict deadline" 直接对应选项 C 中的 "time management"。
Gemini Technologies 的项目要求很严，实习生可以学习如何在**严格的截止日期（strict deadline）**前工作。
Shona: ...examining a company’s financial statements...
原文列举了 "income statement, balance sheet"，这些都属于 Financial training。
Deloitte（德勤）提供审查**财务报表（financial statements）**的经验，如损益表、资产负债表等。
Shona: ...reach out to other business partners and pay attention to networking.
"Networking"（建立人脉）和 "reach out to business partners" 对应选项 A 中的 "make business contacts"。
Kearney 提供接触商业伙伴和关注**人脉网络（networking）**的机会。
Shona: Thanks to the internship experience, I became fluent in it [Spanish].
原文提到 "managers speak Spanish" 和 "became fluent"，对应使用外语。
Vortex 总部在西班牙，Shona 说多亏了这段经历，她的西班牙语变得**流利（fluent）**了。
